description:
The open-source multi-agent terminal where Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Qwen work together as a team — without your source code leaving the machine.

Termpolis is a cross-platform desktop terminal manager (Windows, macOS, Linux) built on Electron + React + TypeScript with node-pty powering the underlying shells. It ships as a native app, code signed on Windows, notarized on macOS.
What makes it different:
- Secure AI-assisted development. Built-in AI Security Center auto-scans every AI prompt against 70+ secret patterns, enforces Gemini paid-tier mode, and keeps an auditable JSONL log of every AI-agent terminal launch — every check runs locally.
- Multi-agent swarm. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Qwen Code work together on a task. A dedicated Claude Code instance acts as the conductor.
- MCP server baked in. AI agents control Termpolis via Model Context Protocol, open terminals, run commands, send messages.
- Transparent routing. Every subtask shows which agent got it, why, and what it cost.
- Activity observability. Every token, every tool call, every message from every agent is visible in real time.
- Intervention controls. Pause, cancel, or steer any agent mid-task without leaving the feed.
- Shared memory. A RAG-backed memory store that any agent can read and write via MCP.
- MCP-native end to end. All four agents speak MCP — no terminal-output parsers, no glue scripts, no bridge code paths.
- Share-ready output. One shortcut from terminal to Slack, Teams, or a PR — see Copy for Slack / Teams / PRs.
Fresh session is offered before Claude compacts, not only after
Claude rereads the whole conversation on every turn, so a long session gets more expensive with each message. Termpolis already measures this on your own traffic (Token Savings ▸ session depth). Until now, the Fresh session button showed up only after Claude had compacted, by which point the most expensive turns were already paid for.
What's new
- An earlier offer. When a terminal's conversation gets long enough that a fresh session would cut the cost per turn by at least half, measured on your own sessions, the pane header says so: "Long session. A fresh one saves 55% a turn." with a Fresh session button. On typical traffic this happens at around 100 messages, well before compaction.
- Same safe handoff. Fresh session works as before. Claude writes a short handoff note into Termpolis memory, quits, and a new session starts from that note. If Claude doesn't print the note's id, nothing is quit. Nothing is typed until the OS reports that Claude has exited.
- Dismiss means not now. Close the offer with ×. It comes back only after the conversation reaches the next depth band, when the saving is bigger.
- Also for a Claude you started yourself. Typing claude in a Termpolis terminal now gets the offer too, both before and after compaction. The fresh session keeps the flags you started it with, such as --dangerously-skip-permissions. A prompt you type into Claude that happens to start with the word "claude" doesn't replace them. A Claude started with an inline account prefix (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=… claude) gets no offer, because a retyped claude would start on a different account.
The offer needs evidence. It stays hidden until your own sessions have produced enough samples at both the shallow and the deep length, and it never shows for a subagent's requests or for a failed request.
